title: Geochem Base Profile
description:
The geochemistry overlay on its own: the analytical surface this repository contributes on top of the CDIF profiles. The analysis events that produced a product (instruments, computational tools, reagents, laboratory, samples analysed), the product-type and licence declarations, the distributions and their parts, and the geochem-specific variable, parameter and coverage shapes.
It imports no CDIF schema and composes nothing. geochemProduct is the composition -- the CDIF core, data-description, manifest and provenance profiles together with this overlay -- and this file is the half of that which gBB authors. Factored out 2026-11-04, following the cdifProfile / cdifCompositeProfile split upstream, so that what gBB contributes can be read, diffed and reviewed without the imported profiles around it.
"Overlay" rather than "additions", deliberately: most of these keys exist upstream and this block narrows them and carries their gBB labels. A pure refinement of a CDIF property is the normal case here, not the exception.
Not a standalone record schema: on its own it constrains an object that carries the geochem surface and says nothing about the CDIF properties a record also needs. Compose it, or reference geochemProduct.

schema:license.title: License
schema:license.description: Legal statement of conditions for use and access

schema:relatedLink.title: Related Links
schema:relatedLink.description: Links to related resources at the product level

items.description: Text description of the measurement method

prov:wasGeneratedBy.title: Analysis Events
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Analysis events. Extends cdifProvActivity (from cdifProvenance) with the generic geochem analysis-event surface: the instruments, computational tools and reagents actually used (schema:instrument); the laboratory; the samples analysed (schema:object); the TAPP the analysis followed (schema:actionProcess); and the session identifier and timing.

schema:actionProcess.description:
The TAPP this analysis event followed, or the workflow as it was performed.
Two forms, after the CDIF plan link (cdifProvActivity; option A of the 2026-11-11 activity-used-resources proposal). A bare {"@id": ...} is the link to the TAPP definition, which is typed schema:HowTo for exactly this reason. An inline schema:HowTo is the workflow as performed; when the event also followed a TAPP, that HowTo names it with schema:isBasedOn. One path finds the TAPP either way: prov:wasGeneratedBy/schema:actionProcess/schema:isBasedOn?. The TAPP link used to be the role-keyed prov:used wrapper {"ada:tappDefinition": {...}}, which is closed off below. Inline TAPPs are not accepted here: none existed in ada2 or ada_subjects when the link moved (measured 2026-11-11), so the reference is the only form.
The reference is SEALED, as the ada:tappDefinition reference was, and so is schema:isBasedOn: a TAPP link names the plan and says nothing else about it.
The base cdifProvActivity already supplies a schema:HowTo here, but its step shape carries only @type / name / description / position / url. A geochem analysis event needs the same step surface the TAPP plan uses -- per-step instruments, computational tools and reagents (schema:instrument), inputs (schema:object), result, parameters and sub-workflow -- so the step items are pinned to tappDefinition's WorkflowStep. Both apply: the base and this intersect under allOf, and neither the base HowTo nor its step is a closed object, so the richer shape adds to it rather than conflicting.
WorkflowStep, NOT WorkflowHowTo, is deliberate. The requirement for exactly one "Sample preparation" step carrying bios:LabProcess lives on WorkflowHowTo, and it belongs to the TAPP plan -- a protocol must say how the sample was prepared. An analysis EVENT records what was done and may legitimately describe only part of a workflow, so referencing the step shape alone brings the structure without that requirement.

anyOf.description: The link to the TAPP definition this analysis followed.
The workflow as performed, as a schema:HowTo.

schema:isBasedOn.description: The TAPP definition this workflow was based on, by reference.

schema:instrument.title: Resources Used
schema:instrument.description: What the analysis used, other than its samples: the instruments, the computational tools actually used (acquisition, reduction, processing) and the reagents and reference materials actually used. One array, the kinds told apart by the Wikidata term each item carries in schema:additionalType -- Q3099911 (measuring instrument), Q7397 (software), Q2356542 (chemical reagent) -- which is the CDIF cdifProvActivity rule. Each item is one of those, or a sealed {@id} reference (the CDIF base admits both, and requires exactly one kind term on an item described in place). The TAPP plan prescribes the generic instruments, tools and reagents; these record the ACTUALS used in this specific run.

prov:used.description:
Not where this profile records what an analysis used: instruments, tools and reagents are schema:instrument, samples are schema:object, and the TAPP link is schema:actionProcess. A prov:used that passes the CDIF core shape (strings and @id references) is accepted and checked by nothing more.
The superseded spellings are CLOSED OFF, so a writer that regressed to one fails, naming the key, instead of passing silently. The role-keyed wrappers carry no @id and the CDIF core rejects them already; these close them off by name, and close off the one old form that does carry an @id -- an item typed ada:TAPPDefinition. Same sequence as the earlier close-offs: the records move first (the ADA stores are migrated before this is published), then the schema.

schema:instrument.description: Superseded wrapper: an instrument is an item of the activity's own schema:instrument.

bios:computationalTool.description: Superseded wrapper: a computational tool is a schema:instrument item of the software kind (Wikidata Q7397).

bios:reagent.description: Superseded wrapper: a reagent is a schema:instrument item of the reagent kind (Wikidata Q2356542).

prov:reagent.description: Superseded twice over (prov:reagent, then bios:reagent): a reagent is a schema:instrument item of the reagent kind.

ada:tappDefinition.description: Superseded wrapper: the TAPP link is schema:actionProcess {"@id": ...}, or schema:isBasedOn on the event's inline workflow.

then.description: A TAPP is not a prov:used entity: link it with schema:actionProcess {"@id": ...}, or with schema:isBasedOn on the event's inline workflow.

schema:name.description: Sample name/identifier as used in the lab.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Per-sample PropertyValue entries (e.g. analysis location); technique profiles constrain these.

ada:spatialRegistration.title: Spatial Registration
ada:spatialRegistration.description: The coordinate system defined ON the sample -- typically a planar thin section -- that image pixel coordinates are registered to. Distinct from the ada:spatialRegistration on an image or imageMap part, which maps pixel coordinates WITHIN one file: this one is the frame those are registered to, and is what lets two images of the same section be compared. Optional, and no record carries it yet.

schema:identifier.title: Session Identifier
schema:identifier.description: The analytical session's own identifier -- the laboratory's run, sequence or batch identifier as generated by the instrument or acquisition software. Sits on the activity rather than the dataset because the session IS the activity.

schema:startDate.description: Superseded: the analysis start is schema:startTime. Rename the key.

schema:endDate.description: Superseded: the analysis end is schema:endTime. Rename the key.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Per-analysis PropertyValue entries (replicates, transect length, ...); technique profiles constrain these.

ada:combinedResults.description:
The reported values this session obtained by averaging or otherwise combining several individual results -- the ROWS of the combined-result table, and the domain that `defines: combined result` enumerates (Rule 7; see the Legends sheet of any delivered TAPP). One entry per combined value, each naming what it combines: "Olivine, sample A, 8 points", "Zircon weighted-mean date, sample B, 236 of 246 spots", "Isochron, sample C, 36 runs".
On the ACTIVITY rather than on a sample, because a combined result names its own sample and need not belong to exactly one -- an isochron over 36 runs is the case in hand.
It is METADATA, unlike a sampling unit, and the difference is worth being clear about because an earlier design got it wrong. A combined result is a statement the record makes about its own contents, so it belongs here. An individual sampling unit is not: the procedure and the analysis can state only the KIND of unit (ada:samplingUnitType), while a particular unit's identifier is a schema:variableMeasured naming a COLUMN in one of the distributions, and the binding from that unit to its target material exists only in the instance data table beside the results. There is therefore no array of sampling-unit objects here; one was added on 2026-09-25 and removed on 2026-10-01 once that was settled.
Analysis-side only: the procedure can say HOW results will be combined (Combination Method, keyed by reported property) but not WHICH were, so there is no ada:combinedResults counterpart in tappDefinition.
Fields keyed `combined result x reported property` -- Goodness-of-Fit or Dispersion Statistic, and Other Statistics -- ride on these rows as per-reported- property values, keyed by the valueName of the column that declared them.

@id.description: Optional identifier for this combined result.

schema:name.description: What this combined value is and what it combines. Required, because a combined result nothing can name gives a field keyed by combined result no row to attach its value to.

schema:variableMeasured.title: Measured Variables
schema:variableMeasured.description: Variable definitions. Extends cdifInstanceVariable (from cdifDataDescription) with additional generic properties. Requires a description with minLength 3.

@type.description: A variable is either a measured VALUE (schema:PropertyValue) or a SPECIFICATION of one (schema:PropertyValueSpecification); exactly which it is decides how a consumer reads schema:value. One of the two must appear. Further type URIs are welcome alongside - cdi:InstanceVariable is the usual companion - so the array is open.

items.description: Human intelligible name for variable that conveys semantics

dqv:hasQualityMeasurement.title: Quality Measurements
dqv:hasQualityMeasurement.description: Quality measurements reported to assess the resource.

schema:additionalProperty.title: Additional Properties
schema:additionalProperty.description: PropertyValue entries describing the DELIVERED DATA rather than the analysis that produced it (extent, dimensions, ...). Distinct from the per-analysis prov:wasGeneratedBy.schema:additionalProperty. Technique profiles constrain these.

schema:distribution.title: Distributions
schema:distribution.description: Generic distribution structure. A distribution is a schema:DataDownload (or schema:WebAPI, inherited from cdifCore) that MAY carry a cdi:isStructuredBy data-structure description (for a monolithic single file that IS the dataset, or a structure shared across bundle parts), and MAY be a bundle whose schema:hasPart lists member files (typed via cdifManifest). The domain file-classification of a distribution / member (e.g. ADA ada:componentType) is added by the extending profile.

cdi:isStructuredBy.description: Data-structure description of a monolithic single-file distribution (the file is the dataset), or a structure shared across bundle parts and referenced from them by @id. One of the four CDIF DataStructure variants inline, or an @id reference. Optional.

schema:additionalType.description: Optional file-classification of this distribution (or, on a bundle, of the whole archive) drawn from the componentType vocabulary (ada:vocab/componentType) -- e.g. "ada:report", "ada:calibrationFile". Generic and OPTIONAL here; the ADA product layer (adaProduct) instead carries the required ada:componentType. Advisory (annotated via schema:inDefinedTermSet), not hard-enumerated in JSON Schema.

UsedComputationalTool.description: Computational tool actually used (acquisition, data reduction, or processing): a schema:instrument item of the software kind.

schema:additionalType.description: Carries the Wikidata kind term, https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q7397 (software), as {"@id": ...}: what makes this a software item of the activity's schema:instrument.

UsedReagent.description: Reference material, calibration standard, or chemical reagent actually used: a schema:instrument item of the reagent kind.

schema:additionalType.description: Carries the Wikidata kind term, https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q2356542 (chemical reagent), as {"@id": ...}: what makes this a reagent item of the activity's schema:instrument.

@type.description: What the material IS, independent of the role it plays in this run (that is ada:reagentRole). schema:DefinedTerm for a material identified by a registry entry (GeoReM, NIST SRM, USGS); schema:Product for a specific catalogued specimen or purchased lot; schema:ChemicalSubstance for a bulk chemical or coating stock.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier (IGSN, catalog number, GeoReM ID).

schema:termCode.description: Registry code for the material on the schema:DefinedTerm path.

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The registry the schema:termCode belongs to.

PropertyValueEntry.description:
One entry of a schema:additionalProperty array: a named value carried on the dataset, on an analysis, or on a sample. The three sites above delegate their per-technique CONTENT to the technique profiles -- which property names are allowed, and with what values -- and this def supplies only the ENTRY SHAPE those names are carried in, so that a placement path such as `schema:additionalProperty[schema:name='Map Area'].schema:value` names something the schema has heard of.
Measured across all 2047 additionalProperty entries in this repository's examples (2026-10-08): every one carries both '@type' and 'schema:name', and none carries a property outside the set below, so the two required keys are measured rather than assumed. '@type' is always a one-element array.
DELIBERATELY NOT SEALED. additionalProperties is left open so a technique profile can add a property without every consumer of this block having to learn about it first -- the same reason the sites delegate in the first place. The consequence is that a MISSPELLED property here still validates; what this def buys is that the register's path checker (amds-ldeo/metadata, loaders/map_subject_keys.py) can now tell a real typo from a node that simply declares nothing. Before it existed, those two were the same report, and 18 correct paths were indistinguishable from a wrong one.

@id.description: Identifier for this entry, so it can be referenced -- typically the CURIE of the parameter it instantiates, e.g. ada:parameter/labxctTAPP/xrayEnergy. Not a resolvable URL, so no format assertion.

schema:name.description: Human-readable label, matching the TAPP Metadata Item where one exists.

schema:value.description: The value. Left untyped on purpose: measured as string, integer and number across the examples, and a technique profile is the right place to pin one.

schema:propertyID.description: URI(s) identifying this property in a vocabulary. Always an array of IRI-reference objects where present; left unconstrained here because the profiles that care already constrain it.

schema:unitText.description: Unit the value is expressed in, as written.

schema:valueName.description: Machine-readable name, for serialization and form binding.

schema:defaultValue.description: Value carried into an analysis from the procedure, where the entry is a spec.
